- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (sentiment > 0.3).  
- Underestimate prices during prolonged downward trends or when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.1).  
- Lag in correction: model often overshoots early in the forecast horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) and then gradually converges — adjust for delayed mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is consistently low or flat (last 3–5 days sentiment < 0.2), reduce forecasted volatility and avoid sharp upward revisions.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment shifts sharply, model should not immediately reverse direction unless supported by price history.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mid-term price stability — consider smoothing out mid-horizon peaks and troughs.
